core_obligations: Assume quasi-regularity and observe that the graded pieces of the ideal are flat because the quotient is flat (proof lines 8004-8007).
Deduce by induction that the quotients by the powers of the ideal are flat (proof lines 8008-8009).
Identify the powers of the base changed ideal as base changes and conclude quasi-regularity after base change (proof lines 8010-8014).
For H1-regularity, use the base change statement for Koszul homology (proof lines 8016-8021).
proof_roadmap: Flatness of the graded pieces and of the quotients by powers (proof lines 8004-8009).
Base change of the graded pieces gives quasi-regularity (proof lines 8010-8014).
H1-regularity from Koszul homology base change (proof lines 8016-8021).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the quasi-regular and H1-regular properties of a sequence are preserved under base change, assuming the quotient by the sequence is flat over the base. For the quasi-regular statement the proof observes that the associated graded pieces are direct sums of copies of the flat quotient, hence flat, deduces by induction and the flat short exact sequence lemma that all quotients by powers of the ideal are flat, and transfers the graded pieces to the base changed algebra using the identification of the power of the base changed ideal with the base change of the power. The H1-regular statement is read off from the corresponding vanishing statement for Koszul homology under base change.
